Good tension to sit with. Let me pull it apart, because "same activity in 3 places" hides two different cases that want two different mechanisms.

**Case A: same *shape*, different bindings.** "Watch TV" in the porch and "Watch TV" in the bedroom are not the same activity — different TV, different volume path, different scripts, different state rules. What's shared is the *pattern*: needs a media_player/dpad/power, state = TV-on + source-in-X, controls shaped like so. Sharing the instance would be wrong (edit the bedroom's TV entity and you'd break the porch). This is template reuse — and notably, harmonia already had this concept: your editor's "Config source: Template vs Manual" with a shared store. That instinct was right.

**Case B: same *instance*, visible in several rooms.** Your Fire TV literally feeds two TVs; a whole-house "Party Mode" or the basement Sonos might deserve a tile in three rooms. Here it genuinely is one activity — one state, one start script — just *surfaced* in multiple places. And we already have the mechanism: any tile on any screen can reference an activity id. Surfacing is a tile concern, not an ownership concern.

Which makes your **option 1 the right storage model**, with one refinement each way:

- **Store: one flat registry** (the engine wants this anyway — routing, select-healing, and exclusivity all key off activity ids), but every activity carries an **owner room** (we already half-have this as `room_view`; promote it to an explicit `room:` field). Ownership answers: whose select routes it, where Home lands, whose All Off scopes it, and *where you edit it*.
- **Edit: in the Room.** The Room editor grows the harmonia-style Activities section — add/edit/delete full cards inline, Add stamps the owner automatically. That's your Setup-Room→add-activities flow, intact.
- **The global "Activities" page doesn't die — it demotes** to an index: all activities grouped by owner room, with an "Unassigned" bucket that flags orphans (that's your "how do I know it belongs?" answer made structural — nothing can float invisibly). Click-through jumps to the owning room.
- **Reuse: templates, not shared instances.** "Save as template" strips the bindings (entities, scripts, ids) and keeps the shape; "New from template" in another room asks only for the slots. That's Case A solved without the shared-mutation footgun — and long-term it's the community story too: people trading activity shapes, not their entity ids.

One nice side-effect worth noting: Case B (one Fire TV, two rooms) is exactly where your device-derived `state:` evals shine — both rooms' tiles read the same device truth, so they can't disagree. Harmony never solved cross-room device contention; evidence-based state mostly dissolves it.

So: flat registry + owner room + edit-in-room + index-with-orphans + templates for reuse. Does that match your instinct? If yes, I'll restructure the Studio nav and Room editor around it (templates can land as the follow-up — they're additive).

This is the right idea, and it's actually the door to the whole endgame. Let me build on it, because there's one architectural decision hiding inside that makes or breaks it.

**Where do sequences execute?** Not on the remote. If the engine ran sequences client-side, a remote losing wifi mid-sequence leaves your TV half-configured, two remotes could race, and a sleeping kiosk can't run anything — this is literally why Harmony sold a hub. Our core thesis already says it: *HA is the brain, the remote is a dumb fast renderer*. So "moving away from mandatory scripts" shouldn't mean moving execution to the client — it means **the user stops hand-authoring scripts; the integration executes sequences itself**, straight from our store.

And here's the part that makes this nearly free: Home Assistant exposes its own script engine to integrations (`helpers.script.Script`). Our integration can take a sequence — stored as an action list in *our* storage — and hand it to HA's native executor. We get delays, wait-for-state, conditions/choose, service calls, full logging, the entire battle-tested semantics, without generating a single script entity or asking you to touch the Scripts UI. The warm-start-safe Fire TV logic (wake only if off, switch input only if needed, never touch the box) is expressible action-for-action. The Studio's ▶ Test button becomes a call to a `harmonium.run` service. And your `script.activity_watch_firetv` keeps working forever, because a "call script" action is just one more action type — the second-class citizen, exactly as you framed it.

**Building blocks** as a nav section is right, and I'd frame its contents as *named sequences with owners optional*: `sequences: { firetv_on: {name, actions: [...]} }` in the config. Room-owned by default (same ownership pattern we just built), but a block like "Everything Off" can be house-level. The Activity card's Start/Stop fields become **pickers**: choose a building block, jump to edit it ("edit →" like the index), or create one inline — with a plain script entity still accepted in the same field for back-compat. Reuse falls out for free: "TV wake" as a block used by both Watch Fire TV and Watch Smart TV, which is exactly the deduplication your two current scripts are begging for. The visual editor is harmonia's action-preset row (Media player / Light / Script / Delay / Wait for / Custom action…) — the one part of your harmonia editor we haven't rebuilt yet, now with a better home.

And the same move sets up the next domino, because you said the magic words — *our storage engine*: the `input_select.porch_activity` helper is next. The integration can create its **own select entity per room** (integrations mint entities natively), seeded from our config — no user-created helpers, ever. And one step further: the integration already stores each activity's `state:` evals… so it can *subscribe HA-side and maintain that select itself*, which retires the hand-written sync automation too. At that point HA objects you hand-maintain for Harmonium drop to approximately zero — the store is the single source of truth, which is precisely the product.

My instinct on phasing: **sequences + Building blocks + Test + activity pickers first** (schema, `harmonium.run` service, Studio section, engine calls the service for `sequence:` starts with script strings unchanged) — and I'd port your two watch scripts into blocks as the proof, doctrine comments and all. The integration-owned select and the absorbed sync automation are phase two — same direction, but they touch the live state machine that's finally behaving, so I'd rather land them separately where we can test carefully.

Want me to start on phase one — and are you comfortable with me porting `activity_watch_firetv` / `activity_watch_smart` / `activity_off` into sequences as part of it (your HA scripts stay untouched as fallback until you delete them)?

You're not confused — you've found a real four-way distinction that the current UI smears into one box. Let me name the layers, because once they're named, every question in your flow answers itself.

**Nouns, wiring, verbs, truth.** An activity has four device-relationships, and they're genuinely different things:

1. **Devices** — the cast list. "Watch Fire TV involves: Fire TV, Samsung Q90, WOL button." Pure nouns. This is harmonia's Setup list with the ★ primary, and its jobs are: the activity's face (primary → icon/entity picture), the at-a-glance answer to "what does this touch?", and — crucially — a **suggestion pool** for the other three layers.

2. **Roles** — the remote-control wiring. A role is a *function from buttons to one of those nouns*: dpad→Fire TV remote, power→Samsung, volume→Samsung (commands) with truth from the soundbar. This is your concept #2, today's `$context`, and it's what `control_target` routes physical keys through. Terminology worth keeping straight: the **keymap** (physical keycode → logical button) belongs to the *remote*, not the activity; what the activity owns is the *role wiring* (logical button → device command).

3. **Actions** — the verbs. Start/stop pick sequences, and sequences stay **global and unrestricted** — your instinct is right. A sequence is a reusable building block; "All Off" touches devices from several activities, and a future "Party Mode" touches devices from none. So no, we don't restrict sequence targets to the device list — we **suggest** them first (device-list entities float to the top of the picker when you edit from inside that activity's context, everything else below a divider). Suggest, never restrict.

4. **Truth** — the state rules. They watch entities — usually the same nouns, so again: suggested from the device list, not limited to it (your Fire TV rule watches the *Samsung* for corroboration — cross-device evidence is the whole point).

And here's the answer to "why have (2) at all if sequences don't need it": **the device list was never for the sequences.** It's for the wiring (roles must point at *something*), the face (primary → icon), the truth (suggestions), and the glanceable inventory. The redundancy you felt is real but benign — entities appear in multiple layers because they play multiple parts, the way an actor appears in both the cast list and the script.

**Your question 4 — multiple activities active — is the deepest one**, and our architecture already answers it deliberately: *truth is plural, routing is singular.* The device-derived state evals can happily say Watch Fire TV **and** Listen to Music are both ON (TV playing, Sonos playing — that's reality, tiles should show it). But keys can only serve one master, so routing is resolved by two singular things: **the view you're on** (each view's `control_target` decides what its keys drive — stand on the TV view, keys drive the TV; on Music, the Sonos) and, for ambiguity beyond that, **the room's routing select** — the last activity you *engaged*. That's exactly why the select survives even though truth went device-derived: it's not truth, it's *attention*. Harmony's "current activity" was the same idea with worse plumbing.

So the Setup v2 UI I'd build, devices-first like your harmonia card: an **Add Devices** list (entity dropdown, ×, ★ primary), where each device row wears **role chips** — auto-suggested by domain (add a `remote.*`, it offers *dpad*; the ★ media player defaults to *media_player/power/volume*), tap to toggle, custom chip for new slots. Storage unchanged: chips compile to the same `$context`; the device list itself becomes a small new `devices:` field the engine can ignore today (and later use to auto-generate the view's Devices section — your scroll-down device tiles, for free). Sequence and state editors get suggestion-first pickers fed by it.

If that model sits right — nouns with role chips, verbs global-but-suggested, plural truth / singular attention — say go and I'll build it.

Neither deserves prime real estate on a Room page. Both moved into **Advanced**, relabeled honestly: *Boot view* ("normally the room itself") and *Rooms hub*. Long-term, boot view belongs per-remote in Remotes & keymaps — noted for that page's visual editor.

**"View order is confusing."** Because the caption was *wrong* — that field is actually the **CH◀▶ / page-key flip order** between views (nothing to do with drawers, sections, or activity order). Relabeled *View paging order* with a blunt hint, and moved to Advanced. And you're right about the real orders: **activities now have ↑↓ arrows** on their cards (order = the order everywhere), and tile/section order already lives in each view's editor where it belongs.

**Layout**: the Room page is now clean accordions — *Hero card* (moved out of the boxed chrome), *Activities* (open by default), *Room functions*, *Advanced* — collapsed state per section.

**Presets/apps — your ur_*.yaml files are the perfect brief.** Look what they prove: launching "Netflix" is `select_source: Netflix` on the Samsung but `select_source: com.netflix.ninja` on the Fire TV; Prime Video on Fire TV needs `KEYCODE_PROG_RED` because the source action is unreliable; Max needs a raw `adb am start`. Same app, four launch dialects. So here's the design I'd build:

An **Apps registry** (`config.apps`) where an app is a *house-level identity* — id, name, icon — and **launch is per-device**, resolved in order: an explicit per-device override → auto-launch (the app's source name appears in that device's live `source_list`, exactly your "in theory HA exposes these") → hidden on that device. Overrides take three forms, in increasing power: a plain **source string**, a raw **HA action** (covers `remote.send_command` / keycodes / adb), or — your instinct — a **`sequence:` building block** for anything multi-step. The Apps drawer then stops being hand-authored tiles: it renders the registry filtered by the active `$context.media_player`, each tile resolving its own launch recipe. One Netflix tile, correct dialect everywhere, and the Studio gets an **Apps** page under Model: app cards with an "auto ✓ (in source_list)" chip per device and an override editor where reality disagrees.

Say go and that's the next build: schema + compiler, engine `apps` resolution in the drawer, and the Studio Apps page.

Fixes shipped and mirrored (all 9 suites green). The preview now **follows your selection** — click Watch TV in the nav and the preview navigates there — and re-injection **keeps the screen you're editing** instead of bouncing home (that was the real "doesn't refresh" annoyance: it *was* refreshing, then instantly resetting to porch). The apps drawer is now **consciously curated**: `include: [netflix, youtube, youtubetv]`, in that order — the registry keeps all ten identities, but this drawer offers exactly three (I checked their Fire TV recipes: `com.netflix.ninja`, `com.amazon.firetv.youtube`, `com.amazon.firetv.youtube.tv` — all correct in the registry). The include list is editable as ordered chips on the `apps_grid` tile. Run the bat when convenient and I'll reload the Astrion.

Now the discussion.

**Workspaces.** Agreed, and the storage is already shaped for it — one store key, one config = one *workspace*. The concept: a workspace is a complete remote app — its rooms, views, activities, blocks, apps, theme, remotes. You might have "House Remote" today and later "Bedroom Panel" or a stripped "Guest Remote," each deployed to its own path (`/local/remote-proto/`, `/local/bedroom-panel/`...) and pinned to different kiosks. The title area (your img 1) becomes the workspace switcher + rename, exactly like an app switcher. Store becomes `harmonium.workspaces` keyed by id, each with its own deploy path; `harmonium.run` gains a workspace dimension. It also cleanly answers "where do house-level things live?" — Building blocks and Apps are *workspace*-level, which is what "house-level" really meant. One design question to hold: are Apps/blocks shared *across* workspaces or copied per-workspace? My instinct: per-workspace, with "duplicate workspace" as the sharing mechanism — cross-workspace libraries are the template store's job later.

**Taxonomy.** You've spotted that our four classes are really **two structural types plus bindings**:

- A **Hub** — a launcher page: optional hero, sections (activities / presets / devices / custom groups), tiles. Your "room page" is a hub *owned by a room*; a "group" (Comfort, Music Library, the Apps drawer) is *the same hub* with hero off and maybe the drawer flag. You're right — "group" shouldn't exist as a separate kind; it's a hub with toggles.
- A **Controller** — a control surface bound to a *target*: D-pad/transport/volume, control_target, passthrough. An "activity page" is a controller whose target arrives via `$context`. And a "device page" is a controller bound to one entity — which we *already generate* (`detail:<entity>` pages) — so "device page" isn't a third kind either, it's a controller with a fixed, single-entity binding and auto-composed content.

The reason four classes exist today is the **physical-key policy** (Power's blast radius: room=All Off, group=page devices, detail=toggle, activity=end). But notice: the policy can derive from the *binding* instead of the class — hub owned by a room → All Off; hub unowned → page devices; controller bound to an activity → end it; controller bound to an entity → toggle it. Same behaviors, zero enum. That's the collapse: **type (hub|controller) + binding (room / activity-context / entity) + toggles (hero, tabs, drawer)**, and every current behavior falls out. Naming candidates for the hub-owned-by-room thing, since "room page" bothers you: *Room hub*, *Launcher*, or just *Room* (the page **is** the room in the user's mind — which your Home-view question already proved). My vote: call them **Hub** and **Controller** in the taxonomy, and let the room's hub simply be "the room."

**"One Watch TV page, passed context and maybe overrides — too constraining?"** It's not only not too constraining — it's *already how it works* and it's the best idea in the system. The single `tv` controller serves Watch Fire TV and Watch Smart TV today: each activity overlays its `$context` (different dpad target, different command map, same page). The escape valves already exist for when it *does* constrain: an activity can point `screen:` at a different controller entirely (structural divergence), and per-activity context overlays handle everything short of that. What we *don't* have yet — and should add when we formalize this — is per-activity **content** overrides on a shared controller ("hide the transport row for Smart TV," "different apps include per activity") — small, declarative visibility conditions (`when: activity == watch_smart`), not new pages. That keeps the Harmony insight intact: one well-designed control surface, many activities flowing through it.

If this taxonomy lands right for you, the migration is gentle: `class` stays in the config as a compiled artifact, the compiler derives it from type+binding, and the Studio's View editor swaps its "Class" dropdown for "Type: Hub/Controller" + toggles. Workspaces are a bigger lift (store schema v2, switcher UI, per-workspace deploy paths) — worth its own round. Which one first?

The distinction to keep: **storage stays a separate screen.** The drawer remains its own view in the config — because it's a navigation target at runtime, and because someday a drawer might serve two controllers (two music controllers in two rooms sharing one library is plausible). Presentation nests; data doesn't. Same move we made with activities-in-rooms: the flat registry is the implementation, ownership is the interface.

Done — Astrion reloading.

And good question: **you can absolutely do it yourself, it's just two button presses in HA.** The Astrion runs Fully Kiosk, whose browser caches the engine file — so after the bat copies a new `index.html` to `www/remote-proto/`, the kiosk keeps running the old cached copy until told otherwise. The two buttons (from Fully Kiosk's HA integration) are:

1. **`Astrion1 Clear browser cache`** — dumps the cached engine
2. **`Astrion1 Load start URL`** — reloads the remote's page fresh

You'll find them under Settings → Devices & Services → Fully Kiosk → the Astrion1 device (or drop them on any dashboard as button cards — worth doing if you'll iterate a lot). The Studio's **"Save + Reload Astrion"** button presses both too, but it saves-and-deploys first, so it's for config edits; for engine-only updates like this one, the raw buttons are the right tool.

When it's needed, for reference: only when the **engine** or **deployed config** changes. Studio-panel changes never touch the kiosk (browser refresh only), and integration Python changes need an HA restart instead. Your one-glance rule: *bat + panel refresh always; Astrion buttons if `dist/` changed; ask me for a restart if `.py` changed.*

v0.18 — all three blockers, done and mirrored to G:\. This is Studio-only, so the deploy is the light one: **run the bat, then just refresh the Studio panel in your browser.** No HA restart, no Astrion reload (dist untouched).

What changed, per your list:

**1. ID auto-fills.** Type "Watch Smart TV" in a new activity and on blur the id becomes `porch_watch_smart_tv` (owner-room prefix + slug). It keeps following the name until you hand-edit the id — then it's pinned, and the hint under the field tells you which mode you're in. Bonus hardening: renaming an id (auto or manual) now really does update *every* reference — tile refs, `when:` visibility conditions, and Set-activity-state steps nested anywhere inside sequences.

**2. Setup first, and searchable pickers everywhere.** Devices & roles now sits directly under the identity row, before Start/Stop — cast before actions. And the entity picker is no longer a scroll-a-gazillion dropdown: it's one box you type into, filtering live by entity id *and* friendly name, with **"This activity's devices" pinned on top**. And you're right about the gap: the engine's tile types there are widget primitives — `media`, `volume`, `transport`, `dpad`, `light`, `climate`... — and every one binds to exactly **one entity**. So "Sonos, but volume lives on the Arc" is literally inexpressible at the tile level today. The widgets exist; the *device* doesn't.

Here's what I think the answer is, and it lines up with your Harmonia card almost exactly:

**Make Device the fourth registry.** We already have the doctrine: activities, sequences, apps — author the thing once, tiles generate from it. A device becomes a registry citizen with three parts, matching your definition:

1. **Identity** — name ("Porch Music"), icon, accent. Your Display Name / Accent Color fields.
2. **Cast + roles** — the entities it's made of, and the wiring: `media_player` → the Sonos, `volume` → the Arc, `power` → whoever. *Same role-chip UI as activity Setup* — deliberately one mental model. This is the whole answer to the multi-entity problem: the device object IS the grouping.
3. **Presentation** — your Card Type "Auto": the renderer resolves from the primary role's domain (media_player role → media card, light → light tile), and Detail Level (summary/standard/expanded) says how much of it shows.

Then a hub's Devices section holds `device` tiles that just point at registry entries — and the same registry pays off everywhere: activity Setup's "add device" adds a *device* (all its roles come along, per-activity overridable — Watch Fire TV can still route volume to the TV even though Porch Music's default volume is the Arc), the pickers' pinned group becomes real devices, and later HA's device registry can *seed* entries (pick "Sonos Arc" in HA-speak → entities pre-filled) rather than replace ours.

On "what should we support" — my proposed v1 renderer set, smallest that covers your house: **media_player** (name + state + volume driving the volume role; transport at higher detail), **light/switch** (toggle + brightness — widgets exist), **climate** (exists), and **remote** as a control-surface-only device (no state to speak of; it renders as a "open its controller / dpad" tile). Covers, fans, sensors-as-attribute-cards: next wave. Detail levels I'd stage too — summary first, standard/expanded after, so we don't build three renderers per domain on day one.

3. **Do devices belong to a room** (like activities do), or are they house-wide with rooms just referencing them? The Arc case suggests house-wide — the basement Sonos already serves the porch.

One entity per device tile is the right cut, because the *page hierarchy already encodes the rest*: the room page is for glancing and poking, the controller pages (Fire TV, Music) are where the compound wiring lives, and activities are where multi-entity orchestration already works via roles. We don't need a device registry duplicating what activities and controllers already know. Device tile = one entity + smart defaults. Done.

So the shape I'd build — one new tile type, `device`:

**Renderer** resolves from the entity's domain automatically (your Harmonia "Auto"): media_player gets the media summary (name, state line, accent dot when active), light/switch get the toggle look, climate gets temp, remote gets a plain control chip. No per-tile widget choice needed — picking the entity IS the configuration.

**Tap** = the domain's obvious verb: media_player → play/pause (with one refinement: if it's *off*, tap turns it on — pause/play on a dead TV feels broken); light/switch/fan → toggle; climate → nudge nothing, it opens (a thermostat has no obvious one-tap verb); remote → opens.

**Long-press** = go to the compound screen. And here's where it gets almost free: we can *infer* the target — if the entity is some activity's primary media_player, hold goes to that activity's view (the Fire TV tile knows about the tv screen because Watch Fire TV declared it). An explicit "Opens" field on the tile overrides the guess. Zero config in the common case, flexible when you want it.

**Volume-elsewhere** never touches the tile at all — that's already solved where it belongs: the room's `context.volume` and the activity's volume role decide who the volume keys drive. The Sonos tile on the porch page just shows what's playing and pauses it; the Arc question doesn't exist at this layer.

**Activities: absolutely.** It's the same gap you found with Start/Stop actions — "Navigate to (after start)" is a dropdown over pages that don't exist yet, and the only way out is authoring a view by hand somewhere else. **Devices: I'd resist creating pages.** A lone device (your light, a fan) doesn't deserve an authored view that goes stale — and the engine *already generates* detail screens per entity: the `detail:<entity>` compositions (power + steppers + chips fed live from the entity's own attributes — hvac_modes, source_list). So the better move is the thing we deferred yesterday: when a device tile has no verb and no inferable page, tap/hold falls back to its **generated** detail screen. Zero authoring, can't rot, and it quietly answers "what does tapping a thermostat do" too. If a device genuinely deserves a real page, that's usually the smell that it deserves an *activity* — and then it gets the button above.

One design choice inside the activity button worth settling: should the minted page be wired as tiles you can freely edit (baked at mint time, diverges from the cast afterward), or should its Devices section be a *generator* like the activities tile — "cast of this activity", always in sync, prune via the activity itself? The generator is more doctrine-pure ("author the thing, never its tile"), but baked tiles are more obvious to edit. My lean: generator, with the escape hatch that deleting it and placing plain device tiles is always allowed. Your call — say the word and I'll build it.

SURESH  2026-07-22T23:43:59.877Z

Give me an example of "baked at mint time, diverges from the cast afterward" and the alternative!

CLAUDE  2026-07-22T23:44:22.628Z
========================================================================

Concrete, with your own porch. Say you mint a control page for **Watch Fire TV**, whose cast today is the Fire TV stick (★ primary), the Samsung Q90, and the soundbar.

**Baked at mint time** — the ＋ writes literal tiles into the new page's config, a one-time copy:

```yaml
# screens.watch_firetv_page (created by the ＋, then it's just... tiles)
sections:
  - label: Devices
    tiles:
      - { id: d1, type: device, entity: media_player.fire_tv_family_192_168_1_65 }
      - { id: d2, type: device, entity: media_player.sts_samsung_q90_porch }
      - { id: d3, type: device, entity: media_player.ma_soundbar_porch }
```

Next month you add a Zidoo player to the activity's cast in Setup. The activity knows about it — volume roles, sequences, pickers all follow. **This page doesn't.** It still shows three tiles, because they're a snapshot from mint day. You'd open the page and add a fourth tile by hand. Remove the soundbar from the cast and its tile *lingers*, pointing at an entity the activity no longer claims. That's "diverges from the cast": the page and the activity drift apart, and you become the sync mechanism.

The upside: those are ordinary tiles. You can reorder them, delete the Samsung one because you never touch it, rename "MA Soundbar Porch" to "Sound", give one a span of 2 — the page is fully yours.

**Generator** — the ＋ writes one tile that *means* "the cast of this activity":

```yaml
sections:
  - label: Devices
    tiles:
      - { id: cast, type: devices, activity: watch_firetv }
```

At render time the engine expands it: one device tile per cast member, primary first. Add the Zidoo to the cast → it's on the page before you've even left the activity editor. Remove the soundbar → gone here too. One source of truth, zero drift. This is exactly how your Activities section already works — you add an activity, the tile appears, and you stopped thinking about activity tiles entirely.

The cost is the flip side of the baked upside: the page has no per-tile handles. Want the Samsung hidden on this page but still in the cast (it must stay for power/volume roles)? Want a custom order that differs from cast order? The generator has nothing to grab — you'd need override syntax (`exclude:`, like the apps tile's `include:`) or you delete the generator and place baked tiles, at which point you've chosen the other model anyway.

So the trade in one line: **baked = you own the page, you also maintain it; generator = the activity owns the page, you edit the activity.** My lean stays generator-with-escape-hatch — start every minted page in sync by construction, and the moment you want page-level art direction, swap it for baked tiles (that swap could even be a one-click "unlink" that expands the generator into its current tiles). Which feels right for how you'd actually use it?

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)

Read it all. This is a good document, and the controller shift is the right one — partly because, and I want to lead with this, **the engine already secretly works this way**. The Watch TV page is not really a page: it's a control surface bound entirely to `$context`, and it already serves *two* activities (Fire TV and Smart TV) with different dpads, command maps, and volume paths because the active activity swaps the context. And the generated `detail:<entity>` screens for lights, covers, climate — those *are* your "fixed controllers," already parameterized, already zero-config. What v0.20 got wrong was minting a *copy* of the anatomy per activity. Your doc names the abstraction we failed to name: there's one Media Player controller, and activities pass data into it. So most of this proposal is cheap — it's a re-labeling and re-plumbing of things that exist, not new machinery. Now the debate points:

**The library and its entries.** Your sidebar lists *MA Media Player* and *TV Media Player* as two entries — that's a telling detail. It says the library doesn't hold raw templates; it holds **configured variants**: "Media Player template + these sections + this apps list" saved under a name. I think that's right, and it answers your own "some can be edited" question: fixed controllers (Light, Cover, Climate, Fan, Switch) are engine-builtin singletons — nothing to edit, they read the entity's attributes. The Media Player controller is the editable one — sections on/off (Now Playing, Transport, Remote, Volume, apps drawer, device list), and you can duplicate a variant when TV and Music genuinely differ. The open question I need your call on: when Watch Fire TV and Watch Smart TV share *TV Media Player* but differ in one detail (say, apps list), does that difference live (a) on the activity as a per-invocation override, or (b) as a third variant in the library? I'd argue (a) for small knobs, (b) when the layout differs — but we should pick where the line is, because it decides what the "controller settings accordion" on the activity actually edits. Editing the shared variant from inside an activity would be action-at-a-distance; the accordion should either be clearly "overrides for this activity" or a "duplicate variant" button.

**Migration falls out naturally.** `tv` promotes to the TV Media Player variant nearly verbatim (it's already 100% context-bound), `music` to MA Media Player. Comfort stays a view. The apps drawer becomes a setting of the TV variant rather than a child page. And custom-authored controller pages should remain the escape hatch — the library covers the 95%, a hand-built view is always allowed. The v0.20 mint anatomy isn't wasted; it becomes the Media Player template's default section set.

**Sidebar + taxonomy: agree.** VIEWS / CONTROLLERS / MODEL / SYSTEM, hub→view everywhere in UI language, `room.porch`→`view.porch`, id defaults from the name slug (collision gets `_2`, same rule as activities). "Type" disappears from views because the type distinction *is* the sidebar section now — with one caveat: the room flag and drawer flag still mean something (key scope, pop-after-pick), so they survive in Advanced rather than dying with the Type select.

**Key-centric view metadata: agree, with sharpened semantics.** "HOME KEY: page:overview" is a more honest name for what Parent does day-to-day. One care point: parent also drives the ⌞ nesting and the Back-unwind ladder, so it stays one field under the hood — we present it as the Home key's destination. For the KEY MAPPINGS block I'd offer per key a small closed set: Back = UI back (default) / device back / nothing. Home = page:<x>. Power = **Smart Power** (default) / All Off / device power / nothing / custom action. And my proposed Smart Power semantics, since you flagged it for discussion: *tap* — on a controller, `$context.power`; on a view whose room has an active activity, end it (with the two-press confirm); otherwise nothing. *Hold* — always All Off for the room. That's mostly today's doctrine made visible and overridable, which I think is exactly what "key-centric" should mean: no new behavior, no hidden class-derived policy.

**The Start/Stop mint flow — you're right, it's a trap.** The fix is that ＋ must open the sequence editor in **draft mode**: a Confirm button that only then writes the sequence, links it to the Start slot, and returns you to the exact card you left; Cancel (or Back) discards the draft and returns you with the slot untouched. Plus a general Back affordance on the model pages that remembers where you came from. Nothing gets auto-linked before Confirm. Same draft-commit pattern should apply to "Navigate to → controller" once the accordion exists.

**Navigate-to overhaul: agree, and it kills the page mint.** Default = controller guessed from the primary device's domain (media_player → Media Player variant for that room if one exists, else the template default; climate → Climate; light → Light), override to any other controller or any page/view. The ＋-mint-a-page button from v0.20 then retires for activities — it only made sense in a world without a library.

If you bless the general shape, the decisions I actually need from you before any code: **(1)** per-activity override vs. duplicate-variant — where's the line, and what does the accordion edit; **(2)** Smart Power semantics as proposed, or something else; **(3)** naming — "Actions" for what's now Building blocks (fine by me; internally they stay sequences), and do Apps and All activities also live under MODEL; **(4)** do we migrate your live tv/music pages into library variants in the same release, or run both models side by side for a version while you kick the tires in Scratch?

Your screenshot actually contains the answer to #1. Look at what's *above* the devices section vs. *below*: the top half (control target, Now Playing, Transport, buttons, Remote, Volume) is 100% `$context`-bound — not one hardwired entity. The bottom section is the only part with real entity ids in it. That's the dividing line, and it dissolves the override-vs-variant dilemma:

**The controller owns only the control surface. The devices section isn't part of the controller at all — the caller brings it.** When Watch Fire TV navigates to the Media Player controller, its devices section is generated from *that activity's cast* — which is exactly the cast generator we already built (primary first, remotes skipped). Watch Smart TV lands on the *same* controller and sees *its* cast. So your worry in {curly braces} — "we still need to feed the device data" — evaporates: device data always flows in from the calling activity, never lives in the controller. A variant never contains an entity id. And "I will certainly want to change the devices" is already solved in the right place: you change the activity's Setup, and the controller follows.

That shrinks what's left to configure to almost nothing, so both of your options survive at the size they deserve:

- **Accordion on the activity (override)** — for the small per-activity deltas: section order/on-off in rare cases, apps list, hide a cast member on this page. Stored on the activity, explicitly labeled as overrides.
- **Variant in the library** — only when the *surface itself* structurally differs (MA Media Player has no Remote pad or apps; TV Media Player does). And to keep variants from breeding: a "Save as variant…" button inside the accordion, so a heavy override graduates into the library instead of being reinvented — you'll end up with two or three, not twenty.

**Power — locked, and it's simpler than mine:** on a view, tap with nothing running = nothing; tap with activities running = requires confirmation to end; long-press = ends without asking. One reading to confirm in passing: on a *controller* mid-activity, Power keeps passing to the device as today (that's what your pass-through chips say) — the confirm-to-end behavior is the view-level rule. If you'd rather Power confirm-ends everywhere, say so, but I believe the split matches muscle memory: on the TV page you're pointing the remote *at the TV*.

**Actions** — done, Building blocks renames.

**Apps as a Preset Library** — noted and parked, and I like it more than you may realize: "named preset lists with a parent group" unifies three things we currently do separately (apps registry, music favorites via `presets_from`, hand-authored preset tiles) into one model — a list of presets, grouped, referenced by controllers and views with an `include`. That refactor slots in cleanly *after* the controller work because controllers become the main consumer of these lists.

So the shape for #1, one line: **controller = named, ordered control surface bound to `$context`; caller passes context + cast; activity accordion holds small overrides; "Save as variant" promotes big ones.** If that's blessed, the build order I'd take: (1) sidebar + taxonomy (VIEWS/CONTROLLERS/MODEL/SYSTEM, hub→view, id-from-name, HOME KEY + key mappings incl. the new Power rule), (2) controllers registry + `controller:` navigation with tv/music migrating to the first two library entries, (3) the draft-Confirm/Cancel fix for the ＋ mint flow, (4) activity accordion + save-as-variant. Say go and I'll start with (1)+(3) — the smallest deployable slice — then (2) as its own push so the migration gets its own chair test.

CLAUDE  2026-07-23T17:39:48.079Z

Good catch, and your confusion is diagnostic — there are actually two separate problems tangled here, and only one of them needs the instancing you're proposing.

**#2 is a migration bug, not a design gap.** Watch Smart TV shows Fire TV in the devices list because the migrated TV Media Player def carried the *hand-baked* device tiles from the old tv page (Fire TV, Samsung, Soundbar, TV Power — literal entities). But we already built the right mechanism: the **cast generator**. A bare `{type: devices}` tile on a controller expands to *the active activity's cast* — that's the "caller passes the data" principle, and it's already engine-side. The fix is just to swap the baked devices section in the tv/music controller defs for the generator: then Watch Smart TV's visit shows Samsung + Soundbar (its cast), Watch Fire TV's shows Fire TV + Samsung + Soundbar, and a future Watch Bluray gets its Zidoo for free — one shared surface, correct nouns per caller, zero instancing required. (TV Power survives as a baked extra row, or moves into the cast as a device.)

**#1 is real, but eager children have a trap.** "Attach controller → create a child per activity" quietly reintroduces the exact thing your polish doc set out to kill: one page per activity. Ten activities, ten near-identical copies; improve the parent's Transport row and no child hears about it. That's the baked-tiles problem at page scale. What your instinct is *actually* asking for, I think, is: **when I edit from an activity, I want the blast radius to be that activity.** So my counter:

- The controller editor gets honest about sharedness: arriving anywhere on TV Media Player shows a banner — **"SHARED surface · used by: Watch Fire TV · Watch Smart TV"** (clickable chips), plus the missing **← back** button (same prevKey mechanism the Actions page got).
- Next to it: **"⧉ Private copy for Watch Fire TV"** (offered when you arrived from an activity). *That* creates your child — named "Porch Watch Fire TV", stamped with its lineage so the sidebar nests it exactly like your tree: TV Media Player ⌞ Porch Watch Fire TV — and re-links the activity to it. From then on, edit away; it's yours.

So: your tree, but children are **born on first divergence**, not on attach. While an activity hasn't customized anything, it shares the parent and the cast generator feeds it the right devices — which, per your own doc, is "most of the time." The moment you want a different section order for Fire TV specifically, one click materializes the child. Apps drawers stay shared by the parent unless you copy them too, which I'd defer.

If you'd rather have **eager** children anyway — attach always instantiates, because predictability beats purity — say so plainly; it's cheap to build and I'll stop arguing. But my vote is: generator fix + shared-banner + back button + copy-on-customize with lineage nesting. Which way do you want it?

**1. Listen to Music card — real crash, nice catch.** Opening it threw a Svelte error and silently ate the card. Root cause: `music` is the only activity without a `confirm_end` key, and the "Confirm before ending" switch was binding to that undefined value — the exact bind-to-undefined crash class we've hit before. Fixed with a function binding, and smoke-studio now opens *every* activity card so no single activity can be the odd one out again.

**2. "Weird devices" in the TV controller — also real, and subtle.** The bare cast generator used *the active activity's* cast unconditionally. You had music playing, so the TV Media Player page showed the **Sonos**. Now the active activity lends its cast only when it actually *targets* that surface; otherwise the controller falls back to deriving devices from its **own default context** — so the TV stock page shows Fire TV + Samsung + Soundbar whether you browse it idle, mid-music, or from the Studio. (What you saw in the Studio tile card — "Cast of activity: —" — is correct for stock, by the way: blank means "the caller decides"; it reads better now that the fallback is sane.)

**On reset/resync**: three levels exist today — **Revert** (top right in the Studio) reloads the last *saved* config, discarding draft edits; **the bat + my reseed** restores repo truth over everything (that's the big hammer — your Studio-saved changes are replaced by the repo build, which is what happened at each deploy); and per-controller, **↺ Reset to stock** on custom copies. Discussing — no code. And your framing closes a loop that's been half-open since the taxonomy rework: if a *view* is a collection of activities/devices/presets, and a *controller* is a control surface, then the thing we've been calling a "group tile" has no business being its own noun. It's a **door**. A nav card.

Here's what I think your model implies, stated back sharply:

**The page side is already true.** A "group page" is just a view — comfort has been a full hub with the same anatomy (activities/presets/devices folds, hero, key mappings) since the every-hub-is-identical rework, and pages minted from a tile now open with everything present-but-off. So "groups are just another page with all the same features" isn't a proposal anymore; it's the current state. What's left is to stop *calling* anything a group.

**The tile side is where the real cleanup is.** Today we have *three* tile types that are all secretly the same thing: `nav` (plain button → page), `room` (image card → page, used on Home), and `group` (live summary "4 entities · 2 active" derived from the target page → page). Under your model these collapse into **one Nav card** with a *style*: plain, image, or live-summary — and style could even default to *auto*: if the target page has device tiles, show the summary; if the card has an image, show the image; else plain. The summary behavior stays exactly as-is mechanically (it derives from the destination's tiles — the door peeks through the keyhole), it just stops being a separate species. Room tiles on your Home overview become Nav cards in image style. Three types die, one lives.

**The workflow** then reads exactly like the activity's Navigate-to, as you say: in a section, **＋ Add device · ＋ Add nav card** — the two nouns a Devices section actually contains: *things* and *doors*. The nav card's concertina holds: label/icon, Style, and **Opens** — pick an existing view, or ＋ create one (named from the label, parented to the view you're standing on, anatomy off). That ＋ mechanism shipped yesterday in v0.24.1; what it's missing is your framing around it — it's currently reachable only by adding a tile and flipping Type to "group", which is exactly the backwards flow you keep catching.

Open decisions I'd want your call on before touching anything:

1. **The merge** — one config type `nav` with `style: auto|plain|image|summary`, engine keeps rendering legacy `group`/`room`/`nav` as aliases forever (zero migration risk), Studio presents them all as Nav cards. Yes?
2. **Style: auto** as the default, explicit override available — or always explicit?
3. **Add buttons**: "＋ Add device · ＋ Add nav card" in *every* section, or only Devices-role sections? (My lean: everywhere — a Presets section might legitimately want a door too, and two buttons is still simple.)
4. **After ＋-create**: jump into the new page (current behavior), or stay on the tile with "edit →" appearing (the draft-flow pattern)? Jumping felt right for pages since there's nothing to confirm — but you've overruled my instincts on flow twice, so: your pick.
5. **The word "group" disappears from the UI entirely** — sidebar subs, hints, role labels ("Devices" role keeps its name; the *pages* are just views). Any place you'd want to keep it?

Good — let's stay in discussion, because your last line is the one that deserves real weight.

**Hero: stays separate, firmly.** The hero is page *chrome* — banner, jump strip, clock — it belongs to the view, not to the tile family. Nothing in the nav-card unification touches it. We agree.

**Legacy: agreed, clean break.** Single user, hard-migrate — `group`/`room`/`nav` become one `nav` type in config, no aliases to babysit. The old names survive only as *styles*, which is where I think your "some of those dropdown items will be useful" instinct points: what was worth keeping about `room` was never its type-ness, it was the image-card presentation. Style options preserve the useful variety without the taxonomy tax.

**Create-flow: your call is right and I'd generalize it.** ＋ on a nav card mints the page and *jumps into it with the drafting banner* — "Drafting **Bedroom** as a new view — nothing is linked until you confirm" — Confirm links `tile.target` and you stay (or hop back, same as Actions); Discard deletes the page and returns you to the tile untouched. And for consistency I'd retrofit the same banner onto the activity's ＋-mint-page path, so *every* ＋ in the product means the same thing: draft → confirm → linked. One state machine, three call sites (actions, pages, and eventually preset lists).

**Now the interesting one: "a nav card is functionally an activity card with a jump to page."** At the engine level you're exactly right, and it's worth saying out loud what the underlying model actually is. Every tile in this system is three orthogonal slots: **what it shows** (label/icon/image/live summary), **what tap does** (start an activity, run an action, toggle a device, nothing), and **where it goes** (a page — as the tap itself, after the action, or on hold/trail). Activity tile = does + goes. Device tile = does + goes-on-hold. Nav card = goes only. Preset = does only. That's the whole zoo in one sentence — and the engine's chassis/adapter design already embodies it.

But here's where I'd push back gently on taking the thought to its conclusion: I don't think we want ONE mega-card editor exposing all three axes, even though the model is unified. Every UX win of the last three days came from the opposite move — *archetypes with inference*: "a device starts with an entity, everything follows"; "an activity starts with a name"; "a nav card starts with a destination." The mega-card is the Type dropdown problem wearing a nicer coat. So: **engine speaks the unified model; Studio speaks archetypes.** Add device · Add nav card · (activities come from the registry). The "All fields" JSON stays as the escape hatch where the full three-axis truth is visible.

**Which resolves your Home-page unease, I think.** The room cards on Home *are* nav cards — but their destination is a different *kind* of view (a room), so two things differ: presentation (image identity, bigger) and, eventually, **summary content** — a door to a room shouldn't count entities, it should say what the room is *doing*: "Watching Fire TV · 22°". A door to HVAC & Lights summarizes devices; a door to a room summarizes life. Same card, summary sourced from the destination's nature. `style: auto` can encode all of it: target is a room view → image style (+ room summary later); target has devices → live count; else plain. Your Bedroom card with no target yet is just a nav card drafted before its page exists — which the new ＋-flow makes a first-class state instead of an accident.

Remaining to settle before I write anything: **(a)** one `nav` type + `style: auto|plain|image|summary` with hard migration — bless? **(b)** archetype buttons "＋ Add device · ＋ Add nav card" in every section, mega-card rejected — agreed? **(c)** the room-summary content ("Watching Fire TV · 22°") — design it now as part of this, or park it as the obvious v2 of nav cards? My lean: park it, ship the unification, because summary-content-per-destination-kind is its own conversation (what's a room's "vital signs"?). **(d)** anything else you want the nav card's concertina to carry that I haven't listed?

v0.25.1 built, green, and mirrored (hashes verified both sides). Both findings addressed:

**The undeletable Porch Climate group.** Not a migration artifact exactly — it's a real custom section sitting in porch's config from earlier experimenting. The bug was mine: a custom group only showed its delete link once it was *empty*, so a group with tiles in it looked permanent. Custom groups now always offer **delete group & N tiles** (the tiles go with it; the devices themselves are untouched), and controller-page sections got the same affordance. One click and Porch Climate is gone.

**Grid density.** The mystery has a clean answer: the engine has always had both knobs — a page-level `grid.columns` (defaulting to **2**) and a per-section `columns` override — but the Studio never exposed either. Porch reads as one column because the room-hub doctrine pins `columns: 1` on it explicitly; your ＋-minted HVAC page carried no grid at all, so the engine's default 2 kicked in. Now the page editor has a **Grid columns** field (blank = 2) and every section — Devices, Presets, custom groups, controller sections — has its own **Columns** input that overrides the page. So HVAC can be 1-col with a tap, or you can keep dense pages dense and loosen just one section.

Deploy is light this time: only `studio.html` changed on the HA side — run the bat, refresh the Studio panel, and that's it. No reseed (config untouched), no Astrion reload (engine untouched).

And the action card is logged in PROJECT.md as a blessed next-round item: scene/script/preset fold into one tap-runs-something archetype that keeps its Navigate-to slot.

**What a room view is:** a room is a place where *activities live*. Porch is a room; that's why it has Watch Fire TV, Watch Smart TV, Listen to Music. A non-room view (Comfort / HVAC & Lights, the overview, Apps) is just a page — a launcher full of tiles you navigate to and back from. It has no state, nothing "runs" there.

Concretely, flipping Room view on changes three things:

1. **It can own activities.** The Activities fold on its editor becomes meaningful — activities you add there are filed under that room, its activity cards live there, and the activities generator tile renders *that room's* activities. A plain page has no activities of its own.

2. **It gets the room's key behavior.** Power on a room means "end whatever activity is running here" (tap = confirm, hold = immediate, idle = nothing). Power on a non-room page just means "switch this page's devices off/on". Home also ladders differently — rooms climb to the rooms hub; sub-pages climb to their room.

3. **It gets its own activity select** — see below.

**"Minted select":** when the Harmonium integration sees a room that owns activities, it automatically creates a real HA entity for it — `select.harmonium_porch_activity` in your case. "Minted" is just my shorthand for "the integration creates it for you." It's the room's memory: it holds which activity is currently running (`watch_firetv`, `listen_music`, `off`). The engine reads it to know what's on (title bar, highlighted activity card, what Power should end, warm-start switching), and `harmonium.set_activity` writes it when activities start and stop. You used to hand-build this as `input_select.porch_activity` plus helper scripts — that's exactly what we retired in v0.17; now it appears automatically, one per room, and it follows the page id (rename the page to `veranda`, you get `select.harmonium_veranda_activity`).

So: if your new view is a *place* where things run — a bedroom, an office — flip Room view on. If it's just a collection of controls you jump into, like HVAC & Lights, leave it off.

Good challenge — and you're mostly right. Let me take the four in order, because three of them dissolve and one is worth defending properly.

**On 1–3: agreed, the "room" flag is a vestige.** We already collapsed the taxonomy once (everything is a hub with the same anatomy, bits switched on or off), and the Room view toggle is the last place where a page has a *type* instead of *settings*. Look at what it actually gates today: whether activities can live there (but every hub already has the Activities fold), what Power means (but that's just an unexposed setting), and where Home goes (but that's already the per-page Home mapping). So the toggle isn't carrying information — it's *duplicating* information we already have, and that's exactly the gyration you're feeling.

Here's the cleaner frame: **"room" isn't something you declare, it's something a page becomes.** A page that owns one or more activities *is* a place where things run. That's an inference, not a checkbox:

- Add an activity to any page → it hosts activities, the activities generator shows them, its name prefixes their ids, it shows up as a top-level "place" in the sidebar. Remove the last activity → it's just a page again. The toggle disappears entirely.
- Power becomes an explicit, visible setting in Key Mappings on every page — default **Auto**, which resolves exactly as today: page owns activities → end-the-running-activity (confirm/hold doctrine); plain page → switch this page's devices; controller → pass to device. But you can override it anywhere, which is what you asked for in point 2.
- Home stays what it already is: the per-page mapping. Nothing new needed.

**On 4: this is the one I'll push back on — but your instinct about remit is half right.** The select isn't storage. The Store already holds everything structural; the select holds one thing the Store can't usefully hold: *live runtime state* — "what is running on the porch right now" — and the reason it's an HA entity is that entities are HA's pub/sub bus, and we're a web page speaking HA's websocket. Because it's an entity we get, for free: the engine subscribing to it and re-syncing after every reconnect and restart; every remote in the house converging on the same truth (start an activity from your phone, the wall panel updates); your own sync automation reacting to it; and it being visible to dashboards, voice, and any future automation ("if porch is watching TV, dim the hall"). If we kept that state private in the Store, we'd have to invent our own push channel to the frontend, our own reconnect/resync logic, and your house would go blind to activity state — the one piece of Harmonium state that genuinely *is* house state. That's re-implementing HA's state machine, badly, to avoid using it.

Where your remit instinct is right: we should mint the **absolute minimum**, and it should be earned, not declared. Which the inference above gives us for free — a select exists *because* a page owns activities, one per activity-hosting page, named after it, gone when the activities go. No flag, no ceremony. (Why not one select for the whole house? Because the porch can watch TV while the bedroom plays music — "what's running" is per-place.)

So the proposal on the table, for your yes/no: kill the Room view toggle; "hosts activities" becomes inferred; Power becomes a visible per-page setting defaulting to Auto; Home unchanged; the select stays but becomes a *consequence* (page owns activities → select exists) instead of a blessing. The words "room", "minted", and the toggle all leave the UI — the only sentence left is "add an activity to any page; pages with activities get a live 'what's running here' entity in HA."

The one wrinkle worth a decision: with inference, a select appears the moment a page gets its first activity and disappears with its last — fine day-to-day, but it means a page briefly having zero activities (mid-rebuild) drops its select and any automation watching it. If that bothers you, the escape is "once a host, always a host until deleted." Your call on which rule feels right.

Today they're computed: the integration reads the config on load/save and mints one select per activity-owning page — so under pure inference they'd spin up with the first activity and vanish with the last. That's the behavior I'd change.

My recommendation: **sticky for the life of the page.** The select is born when a page gets its first activity, and from then on it lives exactly as long as the page does — rename the page and it renames, delete the page and it's cleaned up, but stripping activities out mid-rebuild never kills it; it just sits at "off". Reasons: HA convention is that entities don't flap (automations, dashboards, and history all assume stable entity ids); your sync automation keeps working through any restructuring; and the cost of an idle select is zero. Pure inference is prettier on paper, but entity churn is the kind of purity that bites you at 11pm when an automation goes unavailable because you were reorganizing the porch.

So the full package as agreed: Room view toggle gone, hosting inferred from owning activities, Power becomes a visible per-page setting defaulting to Auto (activity-scope where activities live, device-scope elsewhere, pass-through on controllers), Home untouched, and selects born on first activity + sticky until page deletion.

Exactly — you've just dissolved the last bit of specialness. All Off isn't a system concept at all; it's two different things wearing one name, and they split cleanly:

**The derived layer — free, no authoring.** "Stop what's running" *is* derivable, and it's what Power already does: tap = end the running activity (its own Stop action, with confirm), hold = same thing immediately. That comes from each activity's Stop — the thing you already wrote when you built the activity. No "All Off" needed for this; it's just the Power doctrine.

**The authored layer — a plain Action, nothing more.** The sledgehammer — "put this page to bed" — *cannot* be derived, and you've put your finger on why: it's not the sum of the activities' Stops. Stop sequences assume their activity was running; summing them double-toggles things; and the real all-off usually includes devices no activity tracks at all — the string lights, the heater, HVAC to eco. Only you know that list. So it's exactly what you said: just another defined sequence — *Porch All Off*, *Porch HVAC All Off*, *Porch Goodnight*, whatever you write, living in Actions with the rest.

The bindings table is what ties them together, and it makes the name "All Off" disappear from the system entirely:

- **Power (tap)** — end the running activity (derived, confirm). Fixed.
- **Power (hold)** — *default:* end the running activity immediately (derived). *Or bind it:* run any Action you choose — Porch All Off today, Goodnight next month. Just a binding row like any other.
- Any other key can bind to any other action the same way — Porch HVAC All Off on menu-hold if that's your taste.

So "how do we know what to do with all off?" — we don't, and we stop pretending to. The derived fallback (stop what's running) covers the honest 80%, and the moment you want more, you write a sequence and point a binding at it. The `off` option in the select stays automatic — it's the null state, not an activity — and your authored sequences bookend themselves with *Set activity state: off* exactly like your ported All Off already does.

Migration is then trivial: the existing "off" activity dissolves, its sequence is already sitting in Actions as *All Off* (I'd rename it *Porch All Off*), and the porch gets one binding row: Power (hold) → Porch All Off. The "Page functions" fold vanishes.

That's the whole design: fixed rows for tap-Power/Home/Back, a derived hold-Power default, and everything else is bindings → actions. Say go and I'll build it.

Both designs land beautifully on machinery we already have — let me pin them to concrete shapes, because there's one wrinkle in each worth agreeing on before I build.

## App Strategy — your three layers, mapped

**Layer 1 — Master list** (identity only, ~100 entries, no actions):

```yaml
apps:
  netflix: { name: Netflix, icon: material:movie }
  appletv: { name: Apple TV, image: /local/appicons/appletv.png }
```

**Layer 2 — Device classes** (the platform dialects, with launch sugar):

```yaml
app_classes:
  firetv:
    netflix: { command: com.netflix.ninja }          # sugar → adb/start on the class's launcher
    prime:   { action: remote.send_command, data: { command: KEYCODE_PROG_RED } }
    hbo:     { action: androidtv.adb_command, data: { command: "am start -n com.hbo.hbonow/…" } }
  tizen:
    netflix: { source: Netflix }                     # sugar → media_player.select_source
    appletv: { source: com.apple.tv }
```

Three action forms, exactly as you sketched: `source:` (select_source on `$context.media_player`), a full HA-style action, or `sequence:<id>`. A class entry may override icon/image. **The class entry IS the curation** — no more sniffing the live `source_list` to decide launchability; if the class lists it, it shows.

**Layer 3 — the wrinkle.** You said "a controller points to the device class" — but our *one* apps drawer already serves both TVs through context (Watch Fire TV and Watch Smart TV share `controller:tv`). So the class should ride the **activity's context**, not the controller: Watch Fire TV sets `app_class: firetv`, Watch Smart TV sets `app_class: tizen`, and the apps tile just reads `$context.app_class` (a tile-level `class:` override stays available for hard-wired pages). That keeps the shared-controller doctrine intact and the "filter apps" override stays the existing `include:` list. Studio: the Apps slice becomes Master list + Classes (pick apps from master, fill the action per app), and the activity's Setup grows an App-class chip. Migration: today's per-entity `launch:` blocks compile into a `firetv` class + `source:` defaults into a generic class, master keeps identity only.

## Music Library — categories via lists we publish ourselves

Doctrine stays "the remote renders HA-published lists" — but instead of asking you to build template sensors per category, **our integration does the fetching**: it calls Music Assistant's `get_library` per category (artists, albums, tracks, playlists, radio — favorites-filtered by default) and publishes `sensor.harmonium_music_<category>` with the list attribute. The engine's existing `presets_from` machinery then renders each category as a section of the music library view — and the hero's section-jump strip *already* gives you tap-to-jump plus scroll-spy. I'd add: menu-key cycles sections on library views (your "click the menu key" ask), and swiping already works since sections scroll. Refresh: on entering the view + a slow background cadence.

Two things for you to call: **(a)** which categories are on by default (I'd say Playlists, Artists, Albums on; Tracks, Radio, Genres off — tracks lists get huge), and **(b)** favorites-only as the default with an "everything" toggle per section, or favorites always?

Say go and I'll build the App stack first — registry + classes + engine expansion + Studio editors + migration of your current Fire TV dialect — with Music Library as the second lift once apps are on glass.

4. Errors and fixes:
- **Build nondeterminism**: `lib_ids` was a set → controllers key order followed PYTHONHASHSEED → byte-different identical builds broke hash ceremonies. Fixed: list in views order. (Diagnosed via de1ce0 vs 2062d9 hash flip-flopping.)
- **CONTAINER PARTIAL ROLLBACK** (second filesystem-trust incident): mid-v0.32 the workspace reverted to ~Jul-24 snapshot (classLaunch/heroCycle/sensor.py/normalizeApps gone, mixed with fresh patches). Recovery: on-device `tar czf /tmp/h.tgz … -C harmonium .` → cp into mount → device_stage_files → container hash-match (a5208aba97daba64) → extract → marker-verify → re-apply in-flight batch. Doctrine: G:\ is ground truth; marker-grep before trusting container state.
- **buildHeroNav discarded jumps bannerless**: call site passed [] without banner → CH stepping dead on Apps drawer. Fixed: `buildHeroNav(heroJumps, !!(banner&&enabled&&tabs))` — jumps always register; strip gated.
- **`strip` param shadowed `const strip`** → engine-wide syntax error ("S is not defined" in harness). Found via `node --check src/ui/render.js`; renamed local to stripEl.
- **heroCycle geometry misreads**: spy bottom-rule made stepping land wrong on short/unscrollable sections → S.heroAt position memory, seed from top-visible without bottom rule.
- **Prime Video launch**: PROG_RED keycode obsolete; remote.send_command can't run `am start`. Web-researched (HA community thread): `androidtv.adb_command` with `am start com.amazon.firebat/com.amazon.firebatcore.deeplink.DeepLinkRoutingActivity`; Max moved to adb_command too. Also idle apps drawer was empty (apps.yaml context lacked app_class).
- **Span "2" string**: Studio number input wrote strings; makeTile strict === 2 → `+t.span === 2`.
- **Theme vars "do nothing"**: `.tile.row` hard-coded 78px min-height then 17px .lbl — the row variant bypassed both knobs (user hit it twice); fixed with var()/calc(); LESSON: check every global token against .tile.row.
- **Hero "increments of 50"**: not a bug — self-fit snapping to tile boundaries; explained + fit:false opt-out (harness: 230/260/290 → 230/233/233 fitted vs exact).
- **smoke-music broke on retarget** (old mfav/porch_music_favorites ids) → renamed to m_pl_/harmonium_music_playlists.
- **Music sensors 0 at boot**: fetch beat MA startup → homeassistant.update_entity forced coordinator refresh (10 playlists/1 radio); artists/albums 0 = nothing favorited (legit).
- **tv.yaml indent error** on t_btns2 insert → fixed indentation.
- Container-only stale smoke-device.mjs (device had richer trailing:false section) → adopted device copy.
- Bridge disconnects mid-ceremony → wait and retry (succeeded).

5. Problem Solving:
Established doctrines this window: archetypes over types (device + nav card); hosting is inferred + sticky (no Room toggle; select = published runtime state, minted as a consequence); ONE action grammar everywhere (presets/trailing/bindings/keys); All Off is just an Action a binding points at (derived stop-what's-running is the free default); class IS the curation for apps (dialect via context); libraries/stock are SYSTEM (controllers, app master+classes ride into scratch); snippets are authoring material (localStorage, reseed-proof); hide-unwired $context tiles; CH± = section paging wherever unbound; the .tile.row variant must be checked for every global styling token; G:\ mirror + hash roll-ups = disaster recovery. Remaining parked: Fire-TV-sleeping device-tile state ("Lets leave for now"), App-Power semantics fully (power slot done), per-page layout/type overrides, room-summary nav content, workspaces/backgrounds v2, LLAT rotation, yaml round-trip, Genres category.

You're right on both counts — and since that text is also in the Workspaces page itself, I'll fix it there too. First, the plain-English version:

**"Can be", exactly.** Workspaces and remotes are independent. Every remote shows **Main** unless you deliberately point it elsewhere. Two remotes can both show Main (your porch Astrion and your desktop browser do right now — same world, same pages). A workspace is just a *published world* sitting on the server; nothing uses it until some remote is pointed at it. So: three remotes could run one shared workspace, or one each — your choice per device.

**What "point a remote at one" means.** Every remote — the Astrion, a browser tab, a phone — loads the same URL: `http://192.168.1.87:8123/local/remote-proto/index.html`, and by default that boots Main. To make one particular device live in a different workspace, you open that same URL **with `#ws=bedroom` tacked on the end, once, on that device**. The engine reads it, stores "I'm the bedroom remote" in that device's browser storage, strips it from the URL, and from then on that device *always* boots into Bedroom — even from the plain URL. It's the exact mechanism you already used to provision the Astrion: same as adding `#device=astrion` or `#host=…&token=…` one time. For a future Astrion #2, you'd just set its Fully Kiosk start URL to `…/index.html#ws=bedroom` and never think about it again.
